script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for QQQ. Monday — here is your QQQ recap. The portfolio closed down one point zero seven percent on the session.

Semiconductors got hit hard. Advanced Micro Devices dropped five point one seven percent. Nvidia fell four point nine nine percent. The chip sector is under pressure heading into one of the most critical earnings weeks of the year.

The Nasdaq pulled back sharply on Monday as semiconductor stocks led the retreat. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF tumbled three point seven percent, extending Friday's losses. Broad market sentiment remained cautious ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy decision and a wave of major technology earnings expected later this week.

The top story on Monday centers on Nvidia, which remains the single largest holding in this portfolio at seven point six percent. Shares fell four point nine nine percent, dragged lower alongside the broader semiconductor complex. Despite the session's decline, Nvidia confirmed an investment in Safe Superintelligence, the artificial intelligence startup founded by Ilya Sutskever, and will supply the company with its Vera Rubin systems — its next-generation chip platform. Separately, reports indicate Nvidia is in active talks with OpenAI to help finance a two hundred fifty billion dollar backstop for a planned artificial intelligence data center in Ohio. Analysts note that while these moves reinforce Nvidia's centrality to the artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout, questions around circular investing in the AI landscape are drawing scrutiny. With a fifty-five percent net margin and ninety-six point seven billion dollars in free cash flow, the fundamental story remains intact — but sentiment is fragile ahead of earnings catalysts.

Nvidia fell four point nine nine percent on Monday's session, as outlined in the top story. The investment in Safe Superintelligence and the reported OpenAI financing talks are the two developments to monitor closely. Watch for any formal confirmation from Nvidia on either deal.

Apple gained one point one seven percent, outperforming the broader technology sector during a difficult tape. The stock benefited from relative strength as investors rotated toward large-cap names perceived as more defensive within tech. Wall Street eyes Apple's earnings, due later this week, as a key read on consumer demand.

Alphabet rose two point one three percent, one of the stronger performers among primary holdings on Monday's session. A chart published Monday highlighted how Alphabet gained market capitalization in July while Tesla and SpaceX shed a combined one point two trillion dollars. Analysts are framing this week's earnings as a test of the artificial intelligence trade broadly.

Micron Technology fell two point two five percent. Selling pressure in the memory and semiconductor space weighed on shares, consistent with the broad chip retreat. A published analysis argues Micron stock — up more than seven hundred percent over the past year — still has room to run through late two thousand twenty-seven. Earnings from peers this week will set the tone.

Microsoft gained one point nine four percent on Monday's session, a notable positive in a mixed technology tape. Commentary circulating on Monday suggests the market is unlikely to penalize Microsoft's capital expenditure levels when it reports earnings on July twenty-ninth, pointing to one specific number in the upcoming report that reframes the spending narrative. That report is two days away.

Amazon fell zero point three one percent, essentially flat on the session. The slight decline tracked the modest softness in consumer discretionary broadly. Amazon's own earnings are approaching, and data center and cloud commentary will be closely watched given the sector-wide focus on artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Advanced Micro Devices dropped five point one seven percent, the steepest decline among primary holdings on Monday. The move came alongside Nvidia's losses as semiconductor names faced broad selling pressure. No company-specific catalyst drove the decline — this was sector rotation and sentiment. Earnings will be the next major event.

Tesla slid one point two two percent. The stock has been under sustained pressure throughout July, with published data showing Tesla shed significant market capitalization this month alongside SpaceX. No single company-specific headline drove Monday's move. Watch for any commentary from management tied to production or delivery figures.

Intel fell zero point seven zero percent, a relatively contained decline given the broader semiconductor selloff. Intel continues to lag peers on both performance and narrative. No company-specific news drove the move. The upcoming earnings season will be a critical moment for Intel to demonstrate whether its manufacturing transition is gaining traction.

Three specific data points to watch in the next forty-eight hours. First, the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision, expected this week, will directly affect growth stock valuations across this portfolio. Second, Microsoft reports earnings on July twenty-ninth — the capital expenditure commentary and Azure growth figures will move the artificial intelligence trade broadly. Third, monitor Sandisk's eleven point zero two percent single-session decline for any read-through into memory sector weakness that could affect Micron Technology.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for QQQ. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. The Federal Reserve decision and Microsoft's earnings report are the two events most likely to set the direction for this portfolio in the sessions ahead.
